memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "See that the Kohathite tribal clans are not destroyed from among the Levites. So that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons are to go into the sanctuary and assign to each man his work and what he is to carry. But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die." - Num 4:17-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives careful instructions "so that they may live and not die." Behind the warnings in this chapter is not a harsh God eager to strike people down, but a caring God who is protecting His people. He assigns their work carefully precisely so that they will not come to harm.

This changes how we read the warnings. God's boundaries are not there to spoil our freedom; they are there to protect our lives. Like a loving parent who says "do not touch the fire," God draws clear lines around His holiness for the good of His people. The rules were an act of mercy.

We often chafe against God's boundaries, imagining they hold us back from good things. But God's commands are given by a Father who knows what will harm us and what will help us. His "do not" is always for our life, never against it.

The verse says the priests were to "assign to each man his work." Even the protection came through order and clear guidance. God did not leave His people to guess; He told them plainly how to serve safely.

Trust God's boundaries today. They are the loving fences of a Father who wants you to live, not die — to flourish, not be harmed. His commands are for your good.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see God's commands as restrictions or as loving protection?
- Where have you resisted a boundary God gave for your good?
- How can you trust that God's "do not" is for your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your commands are given in love, to protect me. Help me to trust Your boundaries as the fences of a caring Father. Amen.
